title: Chapter 82 — Protection Plans: The Product, The Economics, The Honest Conversation
intro: How plans work, real repair economics, and the integrity standard for selling protection.

sections.title: The Honest Case
sections.content:
A major appliance repair can cost $300 to $800 or more. A protection plan typically costs $100 to $300 for five years of coverage. The math is straightforward: one repair pays for the plan.

That is the honest case. Present it factually. Show the customer the cost of common repairs versus the cost of the plan. Let them make an informed decision.

Never pressure. Never scare. Never exaggerate. The customers who buy protection plans because they understand the value become repeat buyers. The ones who feel pressured resent the purchase.

sections.title: What Plans Actually Cover
sections.content:
Know exactly what the plan covers and what it does not. Cosmetic damage? Power surges? Food loss? Accidental damage? These vary by provider.

An uninformed protection plan pitch is a liability. A well-informed one is a service. Know the product you are selling.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating protection plan selling, ask:

Does the salesperson present plans honestly — with real repair cost comparisons?
Do they know exactly what the plan covers and excludes?
Is the approach informational — or high-pressure?
Do customers feel they made an informed choice — or a pressured one?
